summary: Naseem A. Hines is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. Hines held posts at the University of Washington (attested 1998) and Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1999).

Nashalla Gwyn Nyinda works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Naropa, Chagpori Tibetan Medical Institute, Shang Shung Institute, Qinghai University, and ITEA, later becoming clinic director at Nyinda Clinic (2009) and president of Chagpori Tibetan Medical Institute (2022).

Philosopher Natalie Depraz studied at ENS de Fontenay-Saint-Cloud and Paris Nanterre University. She founded the Rouen School of Phenomenology (2018) and held posts at Rouen, Galatasaray, Paris Nanterre (professor, 2023), and the University of Bucharest (researcher, 2023–2026).
Natalie Gummer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She held a post at Harvard University (attested 2001) and was appointed professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Stephan V. Beyer, and also studied with Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Lengden, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.

Natalie Quli specializes in Buddhist and religious studies, having studied at Cal Poly Humboldt and the Graduate Theological Union. She holds the Yehan Numata Professorship of Buddhist Studies at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and the Numata Center.
Historian Natalie Rothman studied at the University of Michigan from 1999 to 2006. In 2006, she joined the faculty at the University of Toronto.

Nataliya Yanchevskaya works in Indology and linguistics. A former PhD candidate at Harvard University (attested 2009), she has served as a Lecturer in Sanskrit at Princeton University (attested 2016–2026).

Indologist Natalya Julianovna Lubotskaya studied at Moscow State Pedagogical University (~1950–1955). From 1957 to 1976, she served as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Natalya Mikhailovna Sazanova was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She graduated in history from Moscow State University (~1949–1954), where she began teaching in 1958 and became a professor in 1989.

Natalya Vasilyevna Dyakonova specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Saint Petersburg State University, she held posts at the Ukrainian Oriental Institute, the Institute of Oriental Studies, and the State Hermitage Museum.

Natasha Heller is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who completed her PhD at Harvard in 2005. She held appointments at UC Berkeley, UCLA, and became Associate Professor at the University of Virginia in 2017.

Natasha Reichle specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley under Joanna Gottfried Williams, having also studied under Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Alan Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.
Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who completed her PhD under Hans T. Bakker at the University of Groningen, where she also held an academic post from approximately 2012 to 2018.
Nathan Brown was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and Japanology. He studied at Williams College and Newton Theological Institution, and founded the American Baptist Missionary Union in 1837.

Nathan Katz works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He held a position at the University of South Florida (attested 1993) and served as professor and chair of religious studies at Florida International University (attested 2003).

Nathan McGovern specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. McGovern held posts at UC Santa Barbara, Dalhousie University, the University of Munich, and served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Whitewater (attested 2016–2021).

Nathan Sivin was a Sinologist and historian educated at DLI, MIT, Harvard, and Kyoto University. He taught at MIT (1966–1977), served as professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–2006), and was an honorary professor at the Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Nathan Söderblom worked in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Uppsala, the Sorbonne, and the EPHE, he held chairs in the history of religion at Uppsala (1901–1912) and Leipzig (1912–1914) and served in the Church of Sweden.

Nathan W. Hill works in linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology, studying under Leonard van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff, and earning an AB at Harvard. He held posts at SOAS, Trinity College Dublin, NYU, and visiting professorships at Berkeley and Oxford.
